title: A live-imaging protocol for tracking intestinal stem cell divisions in the Drosophila melanogaster pupal midgut
author: Wu, Tang, et al.

steps.title: Activate UAS expression
steps.instruction: Keep experimental pupae at 29 °C for 2 days before imaging to inactivate Gal80^ts and activate UAS‑driven constructs; note that development proceeds ~1.3 × faster at 29 °C than at 25 °C.

steps.title: Collect and stage pupae
steps.instruction: Pick late third‑instar larvae (≈30 per vial) with a brush, transfer to fresh vials of standard cornmeal food and incubate at 25 °C; collect white pupae (0 h APF) from these vials every 30 min, place each batch in a new vial, record collection times, and continue incubation at 25 °C. Use pupae aged 46–52 h APF (at 25 °C) for experiments.

steps.title: Select female larvae
steps.instruction: Transfer late third‑instar larvae to PBS, examine under a microscope and discard any larva showing white transparent testis dots (male); retain only larvae lacking these dots (female).

steps.title: Prepare Live Imaging Buffer (LIB)
steps.instruction: In a sterile laminar‑flow hood at 25 °C, combine 8.5 mL Schneider’s Drosophila medium, 1.5 mL fetal bovine serum, and 2 mg human insulin in a 15 mL sterile centrifuge tube; mix well and adjust pH to 7.0 with 1 M NaOH. Aliquot 5 mL of this LIB into ten 1.5 mL tubes (500 µL each) for immediate use; reserve the remaining 5 mL for gel preparation. Store the 500 µL aliquots at 4 °C for up to one week.

steps.title: Prepare Live Imaging Gel (LIG)
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 g gelatin to the 5 mL LIB reserved for gel, heat on a metal bath at 50 °C for 5 min until fully melted, then dispense 500 µL of the molten LIG into ten 1.5 mL tubes. Store the aliquots at 4 °C (usable for one week).

steps.title: Assemble live‑imaging dish
steps.instruction: Heat the metal bath to 37 °C (or up to 40 °C if needed) and melt the LIG for 10 min. Using a glass cutter, split a 22 mm × 22 mm coverslip into two equal pieces (≈0.14 mm thick). Pipette 10 µL of melted LIG onto a Lumox dish, immediately cover with one 11 mm × 22 mm pre‑cut coverslip; repeat on a second spot, placing the two coverslips ≈5 mm apart.

steps.title: Quantify fluorescence in Fiji
steps.instruction: Open the time‑lapse image stack in Fiji/ImageJ, select the region of interest (ROI) for each cell (progenitor, daughter ISC, and EMC) in the Pros::GFP green channel, measure area fluorescence intensity, and subtract background measured from three adjacent regions. Multiply each cell’s ROI area by its background‑corrected intensity to obtain the Pros amount per cell.

substeps.instruction: Select ROI for each cell based on cell boundaries.
Measure green‑channel intensity of each ROI in projected z‑stack images.
Determine average background intensity from three nearby regions and subtract from ROI values.
Calculate Pros amount by multiplying ROI area by corrected intensity.

description:
The protocol below uses Drosophila pupae with the following genotype: esg-Gal4, 10xUAS-Myr::tdTomato/+; Pros::GFP/+. Red 10xUAS-Myr::tdTomato is expressed in esg+ progenitor cells2 and green Pros::GFP is expressed in pupal enteroendocrine (EE) cells.1,3
esg-Gal4,tub-Gal80ts, 10xUAS-Myr::tdTomato/+; Pros::GFP/+, enables 10xUAS-Myr::tdTomato and other UAS driven construct expression under the control of temperature.4 To study real-time expression and localization of other proteins in the midgut, fluorescently tagged proteins can be constructed using the knock-in method.5 In the study by Wu et al., UAS-RNAi lines were crossed into this system to knock down genes of interest exclusively in esg+ progenitor cells. To inactivate Gal80ts and activate UAS-mediated gene expression, experimental samples were kept at 29°C for 2 days prior to experimentation. Note that pupal development is approximately 1.3 times faster at 29°C than at 25°C.6
